Elecbits is already inside a large opportunity. The next step is to go deeper.

Elecbits today works with customers such as Schneider Electric, Panasonic, Motherson, JioThings and many more, while a growing set of new accounts is entering the pipeline. Together, these companies represent a large electronics wallet.

The more important part

The more important part of the story is how these relationships deepen over time.

Customers include
Schneider ElectricPanasonicMothersonSiemensValeoTeslaPaytmOla ElectricAtherEscorts KubotaJSWJioThingsand many more

A customer may enter through either design or manufacturing, but the relationship naturally expands in both directions.

Design-led entry

Design-led customers increasingly consolidate manufacturing with Elecbits as their products require customisation, BOM optimisation and ongoing engineering support.

Manufacturing-led entry

Manufacturing-led customers often move into design as products require upgrades, new variants and subsequent generations.

Over time, both pathways converge
A deeper design + manufacturing relationship

Schneider Electric and JioThings already show how this plays out: start with a product or smaller program, execute well, and expand into higher volumes, additional products and a larger part of the customer relationship.

This creates two reinforcing growth engines.

Design / ODM

Elecbits designs and develops the product. Once a platform is proven, it can scale through higher volumes, adjacent products and reuse across multiple customers.

Box build

Customers bring existing products to Elecbits for manufacturing. As the relationship develops, Elecbits can take on additional programs while also supporting customisation, BOM optimisation and future product generations.

The rest of this document follows that journey: from the size of the customer opportunity, to how individual relationships expand, to the two growth engines, and finally to a bottom-up customer-by-customer view of what that opportunity could become.

Design ↔ Manufacturing→More products→Higher volumes→Deeper customer relationships

Proof that relationships compound

Start with one program. Deliver. Earn the next one.

Schneider Electric and JioThings show the same pattern: Elecbits entered through smaller mandates, executed, and has since received larger POs and broader programs. The orders already in hand are the proof; the forecasts and tender enquiries below are the next layer of growth, not the starting assumption.

The same expansion motion, repeated across products

Design once. Prove it. Scale it across customers.

Elecbits has 13 developed product families. Growth comes from three repeatable levers: higher volumes on existing programs, reuse of proven designs with new customers, and new product families entering through the live funnel.

A second route to deepen customer value

From a product relationship to more of the manufacturing stack

Box build gives Elecbits another route to expand: scale programs already in production, convert qualified new programs, and move a broader named funnel into production over time. Each layer is modeled at only a portion of the customer’s estimated box-build wallet.

Sizing approach

Electronics wallet (i): The default view uses 30% of revenue as a starting point for electronics-heavy businesses. Actual electronics intensity varies by product mix; utilities and telecom operators are adjusted lower because electronics is primarily purchased as equipment. Use the slider to test different assumptions.

Revenue: Latest reported full-year revenue available for each company. For global groups, the India view includes operating entities and excludes R&D and shared-service centres; international accounts use consolidated group revenue.

Confirmed orders: Where the page says “PO received” or “orders received”, this refers to customer purchase orders already received by Elecbits. These are not derived from the wallet-share assumptions below.

Opportunity build-up: Design / ODM and box-build figures for FY28 to FY30 are Elecbits’ bottom-up customer-by-customer opportunity estimates. Modeled penetration is Elecbits revenue as a share of annual demand for the relevant product or estimated box-build wallet. Confirmed POs are separately identified and are not treated as modeled wallet share.

Sources: Company filings and annual reports. FX conversion uses USD 1 = INR 90. Elecbits FY26 actuals, FY27 to FY30 order book projections, pipeline and account relationship status are based on company inputs.
